title: Commotio Retinae: Berlin's Edema Decoded
summary: Commotio retinae, commonly known as Berlin's edema, is a transient retinal whitening occurring after blunt ocular trauma. While often self-limiting, it requires careful differentiation from sight-threatening injuries like retinal detachment or choroidal rupture.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Commotio retinae is a traumatic retinopathy characterized by opacification of the outer retina (photoreceptor outer segments) and RPE. Pathophysiologically, it involves disruption of the photoreceptor outer segments and subsequent extracellular edema. When the macula is involved, it is specifically termed 'Berlin's edema'. The whitening is NOT due to true intraretinal edema, but rather scattering of light from damaged photoreceptor disks.

sections.title: Clinical Features
content: Reduced visual acuity (variable).
Central scotoma if macula is involved.
Whitening appears within hours of injury.
Resolution typically occurs within 3-4 weeks.
May progress to RPE mottling or atrophy (late stage).

rows: Cotton wool spots, history of systemic trauma

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 1: Dilated fundus examination (indirect ophthalmoscopy).
Step 2: OCT Macula (look for hyper-reflective outer nuclear layer).
Step 3: B-scan USG (if vitreous hemorrhage obscures view).
Step 4: Dilated exam 1-2 weeks post-injury to rule out RRD.

sections.title: Red Flags: Traumatic Emergency
content: New onset flashes (photopsia) or curtains (RD).
Severe pain (IOP spike or rupture).
Presence of subretinal fluid on OCT.
Peripheral retinal breaks.
Vitreous hemorrhage obscuring the fundus.

content.explanation: R-Red reflex, E-Examine periphery, T-Tension (IOP), I-Imaging (OCT), N-Near-peripheral breaks, A-Advise follow-up.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Fluorescein angiography is typically normal (no vascular leakage).
The whitening is transient and typically resolves with RPE pigment changes.
If visual acuity does not improve after 4 weeks, consider occult macular atrophy.
Always document the extent of whitening relative to the fovea.

sections.title: Management Strategy
content: Step 1: Observation is the gold standard for isolated commotio retinae.
Step 2: Rule out associated sight-threatening complications (RD, choroidal rupture).
Step 3: Patient education regarding signs of retinal detachment (flashes, floaters).
Step 4: Serial OCT monitoring until normalization of the ellipsoid zone.
